collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS — DISABILITY AND HUMAN DIVERSITY (DIV-01..50, draft for the owner, 2026-11-15)
Disabled villagers, chronic illness and every kind of body, skin, hair and face: wheelchairs with real wheels, crutches, canes, ear trumpets, signs and lenses made from island materials; good days and hard days; competence, humor and opinions. Sometimes the difference is the story. Often it's just part of the scenery.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. Edit anything and send it back; nothing ships until you approve.

collection.description: A deaf healer's patient keeps telling the story of a sore shoulder while facing the wall: turn them around, or just examine it.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: (subject) is deaf and one of the village's best healers. (subject.He/she) listens with (subject.his/her) eyes and (subject.his/her) hands: how someone breathes, where they flinch, what their face does when (subject.he/she) presses. Today (friend) has come in with a sore shoulder and has not stopped talking, mostly while facing the wall, explaining the whole story of how it happened.

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: (subject) gently turns (friend) to face (subject.him/her) and signs and says, "Again, please. Facing me." (friend) apologizes and starts again. Halfway through, (subject) presses a spot on the shoulder, and (friend) yelps. "There," says (subject), satisfied. "Also, you fell off the roof, not out of a tree. I can tell from the bruise." (friend) is astonished and slightly caught out.

o2__fx.name: Outcome B
o2__fx.text: (subject) lets (friend) talk to the wall and gets on with it. By the time the story's over, (subject) has already found the problem, strapped the shoulder and made up a poultice. (friend) turns around. "Did you get all that?" (subject) smiles. "None of it. But your shoulder told me everything."
